Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the single-threaded follow-ups we discussed around Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) and streaming behavior for Acme's real-time assistant use case: 

Summary of key requirements you confirmed:
- TTFT target: <= 120ms for first token on average (p95 goal <= 200ms) for short prompts (~50 tokens)
- Sustained throughput: ~400 reqs/sec across your fleet during peak (US region)
- Concurrency: typical concurrency ~150 concurrent streams, spike to 400 for short periods
- Streaming transport: prefer SSE for browser integrations, websocket for mobile/native clients
- Chunk cadence: small initial chunk within TTFT, then subsequent chunks at ~120–250ms cadence to keep UI responsive
- Fallback behavior: graceful degrade to non-streaming 200–400ms latency if streaming channel unavailable

Action items I committed to on the call:
1) Share an SLO matrix and network/architecture notes that map to these targets (attached PDF + diagram).
2) Run a quick in-house spike on our side to validate TTFT for the model variants you liked and share the measured p50/p95 numbers.
3) Align on a short technical POA for your dev team (sample SSE/WebSocket client snippets + recommended chunking settings).

Next meeting suggestion: 30 min tech sync next Tuesday to review measurement results and confirm any config changes.

Attaching: SLO_requirements.pdf (draft), network_arch_diagram.png

If any of the bullets above are off, let me know and I will update.

Best,
Aditya

Thanks for the clarifications — noted. A few follow-ups inline plus the technical POA: 

- TTFT targets: we'll run the spike against the model family you tested (LlamaX-13B-quant) and prioritize round-trip for an SSE initial event under 150ms p50, aim p95 <= 250ms. I will include both cold and warm KV-cache numbers.

- Bursty traffic: Redwood Dedicated supports burst capacity mapping; we can tolerate short 5–10 minute windows up to 2x committed capacity with autoscaling policies. I will surface a recommended commit level versus burst allowance in the pricing note.

- Session KV cache: our runtime supports sticky KV cache within a routing session; across replicas we rely on a shared cache tier (we'll detail options: prefix caching, CDN-edge cache for static context, or an in-memory shared layer). See page 2 of the attached SLO_requirements.pdf for tradeoffs.

Technical POA (deliverables I'm attaching/doing this week):
A) Measurement spike (Redwood infra team) — will provide a CSV with p50/p95 TTFT, p50/p95 subsequent chunk cadence, and throughput at concurrency levels 150/300/400.
B) SSE/WebSocket sample snippets — small drop-in JS/Node examples that show how to request an initial token as early as possible and buffer/display subsequent chunks at 120–250ms cadence.
C) Network notes — recommended client TCP/TLS keepalive, load balancer settings, and expected NAT/timeouts to avoid stream resets.

Proposed time: Tue Apr 9, 11:00–11:30 PT for the technical sync. I'll send a calendar invite; please confirm.

Thanks — attaching the updated SLO_requirements.pdf with an extra appendix mapping to autoscaling behavior.

Best,
Aditya
